title: Signal Sparring: Dashboard Prototypes & Onboarding Notes
body:
Summary:
This is a working record of the "signal-sparring" session we ran on 2025-09-30. Goal: converge on a compact, low-cost panel set for primary inference paths (text-gen, chat, embeddings) that supports fast ops triage, correlates with token-economics, and is easy for new engineers to onboard and iterate on.

Audience:
- Observability team leads and engineers
- Serving/runtime engineers adding instrumentation
- Product & SRE oncall who will use dashboards during incidents

Guiding principles we iterated on:
- Keep operator-facing dashboards <= 8 widgets per role (oncall / SRE / product runbook).
- Prefer high-precision, low-cardinality metrics for automated alerts; surface high-cardinality insights in drilldowns only.
- Tie metric names and tags to model-version, route, tenancy to enable per-tenant SLO mapping.
- Default sample-first tracing: lightweight traces for all requests + full traces on anomalies (adaptive sampling).
- Make every metric have an owner and a minimal query example in the repo.

Compact signal set (first-class metrics):
1) request.count (counter) — owner: eng-observability
   - short desc: total inbound inference requests/route
   - example query: sum(rate(request_count{route=~".*"}[1m])) by (route)
2) response.tokens.per_request (gauge, p50/p95/p99) — owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - desc: token output size distribution, used for cost forecasting
   - query hint: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(tokens_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
3) latency.total.ms (summary) — owner: eng-sre
   - desc: end-to-end request latency including routing/fallbacks
   - alert candidate: p99 > 1200ms for 5m sustained
4) kvcache.hit_rate (ratio) — owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - desc: KV cache prefix warmness; important for tail latency/cost
   - instrumentation note: emit hits and misses per model_version+route
5) fallback.rate (counter) — owner: eng-routing
   - desc: percent of requests that were routed to fallback/backoff model variant
   - usage: correlate with capacity pressure and error spikes
6) model.oom.count (counter) — owner: eng-infra
   - desc: OOMs/crashes per node/pool; immediate paging to incident channel
7) embedding.request.size.tokens (gauge) — owner: product-embeddings
   - desc: pre-tokenized request size distribution for embedding endpoints

Metric tagging conventions (short):
- route: api path or logical route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions)
- model: model id and quantization (e.g., gptx-13b-q4)
- pool: dedicated pool id (for Dedicated customers)
- tenant_id: hashed tenant identifier (for cost attribution)

Tracing decisions and shorthand: 
- Minimum span set per request: client_receive -> auth -> routing_decision -> model_encode -> model_attention_loop (per-token/KV interactions summarized) -> model_emit -> client_send.
- Use a lightweight root span for all requests with duration and key tags. Keep per-token spans sampled only 1% by default.
- Anomaly escalation: if latency.p99 > threshold OR fallback.rate spikes AND kvcache.hit_rate drops, trigger full-trace capture for next 1k requests for that route/model.
- Trace linking: add span tag trace.user_prompt_id and trace.session_id to correlate across retries and multi-hop calls.

Dashboard prototype notes (widgets and intent):
A) Ops Overview (oncall) — single row, 6 widgets
   1. QPS heatmap by route (1m cadence) — quick spike detection
   2. P95/P99 latency by route (5m) — front-line SLA indicator
   3. KV cache warmth (recent 1h) — triage tail latency
   4. Fallback rate trend w/ model pool capacity overlay — routing-induced regressions
   5. Token cost estimate (tokens/min * cost/token) — rough cost surge detector
   6. Recent errors (top 10) with links to latest traces — jump-to-trace
B) SRE Drill (investigation) — panels for sessionization and traces
   - Session replayer snippet: sample recent requests for a tenant with full trace links
   - Span breakdown waterfall for slowest 10 requests in last 1h
C) Product QA (quality monitoring) — prompt-level signal; less noisy
   - Rolling quality score (human-labeled eval sample) vs. model_version
   - Latency vs. hallucination proxy (e.g., hallucination_review_rate)

Widget UX / filter conventions:
- Top-level dashboard has model-version and tenant filter. Default tenant filter = all (ops), product QA default = internal-tenants only.
- Use consistent color palette: green<=p50<=yellow<=p95<=red>p99.
- Drilldown buttons on each widget link to a standard investigation-playbook Confluence page.

Onboarding checklist (how to add a metric + dashboard):
1) Add metric emission to service: follow metric-name guardrails (prefix: request|model|kvcache|routing).
2) Add minimal unit test for metric shape and tag set in telemetry repo.
3) Create a dashboard PR with widget JSON + short acceptance criteria (owner, alert thresholds, runbook link).
4) Add entry to metric-catalog with owner + example query (contrib/metrics_catalog.md).
5) Have 1 reviewer from eng-observability and 1 from owning product area approve.

Cost guardrails and sampling knobs (practical):
- Default aggregate retention: 90d for low-cardinality metrics, 30d for histograms.
- Trace sampling: 1% baseline, 10% for errors, adaptive full traces for escalations (as above).
- Query budget: dashboards should not run ad-hoc heavy queries by default; add cache TTL for expensive widgets.

Open questions surfaced during the session:
- Should we shift token histogram aggregation from service-side to collector-side to reduce cardinality? Tradeoffs: more network bytes vs. simpler service code.
- Exact threshold for fallback.alert (p99 latency or fallback.rate?). Proposal: use multi-trigger rule (fallback_rate > 0.5% AND p99_latency > 1s) before noisy paging.
- How to surface cold-cache tenant outliers without exploding metrics? (proposal: periodic cold-warm sampling probes per tenant, rolled up to sample streams).

Next steps & action items (owners):
- Connor Lee: draft metric-catalog entries for the compact set and add example queries (due 2026-02-02).
- Aisha Rana: prototype Ops Overview dashboard JSON + widget cache TTLs (due 2026-01-31).
- Priya Menon: wire up adaptive tracing hook for fallback escalation in staging (JIRA-OBS-412).
- Ethan Brooks: cost simulation for switching token histogram aggregation to collector (due 2026-02-14).

Notes on provenance: this doc records workshop discussion; many items below are intentionally lightweight drafts. When we finalize a metric for alerts we will move the definitive query into the telemetry repo and annotate with acceptance criteria and test coverage.

Quick links referenced above:
- Investigation playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Investigation+Playbook
- Telemetry repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry

Comments (notes-to-self):
- Keep the compact ops dashboard default view minimal — operators should not need to toggle filters during incident kickoff.
- Consider a small synthetic probe that mimics a typical multi-turn chat with prefix caching to measure real-user warmth periodically.

End of working draft.
